{"B_expression":"-1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))**2)","C_expression":"-1/2","derivation":"Start from the host formula g = r/2 + chi_r*chi_u*(r^2*B + u*r*C). The whole residual is E = 2(1+u)*g + g^2 - r. Expanding E to leading orders in (r,u): the O(r^2) pure term is r^2/4 + 2*r^2*B, and the O(ur) cross term is ur*(1 + 2C). Setting B(r) = -1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))^2) (the source exact-root correction, smooth for r > -1, which covers the evaluation domain |r| < 1/2) cancels the pure remainder to all orders in r when u=0. Setting C = -1/2 (a smooth constant) cancels the leading O(ur) cross term. The remaining leading errors are O(ur^2), O(u^2*r), and O(r^3), all of strictly higher total degree than the uncorrected O(r^2) + O(ur). Both bodies are C-infinity on an open neighborhood of the closed outer rectangle since sqrt(1+r) > 0 throughout r > -1/2 and -1/2 is a constant.","inspect":[]


  ,"note":"B uses the source-only exact-root quotient; C is the constant -1/2 cancelling the leading u*r cross term. Both are smooth on the required domain. This is a local coefficient-field construction for the fixed two-slot covariance quotient; it does not establish global NS admissibility, all-order PDE estimates, or any theorem beyond the local algebraic cancellation. A successor should verify that the numerical residual actually decreases in the u != 0 rows on the next stage, and that the chi transition regions remain stable (no sign changes or blow-ups near |r| ~ 1/2 or |u| ~ 1/4)."}
